lead_with.title: Partner, not competitor
lead_with.text: Enzymicals doesn't make APIs. It **adds a biocatalysis toolbox** to Siegfried's chemistry: enzyme screening, enzyme engineering, chemo-enzymatic route design, then **tech transfer into Siegfried's own reactors**. Siegfried keeps the customer and the manufacturing.

lead_with.title: Fill the new capacity with better routes
lead_with.text: Siegfried's CEO says the 2026 acquisition is about **unlocking capacity for new, high-volume business**. Enzymatic steps can cut process steps, solvents and waste on high-volume APIs, helping win and keep that business.

lead_with.title: Low-risk start
lead_with.text: Offer a **feasibility screen on one route or intermediate** (mg scale), with a clear path **mg → ton**. No capex, no headcount, a fixed scope that ops and R&D can both approve.

person.name: Ramzahn Soleymani-Alizadeh
person.text: Listed on LinkedIn as **Ramzahn Alizadeh**, **Associate Director, Strategic Operations** at Siegfried (title per Streak/LinkedIn). His **site, tenure, education and earlier roles are to be confirmed**: the LinkedIn profile can't be read from outside and no public bio was found. His **@siegfried.ch** email is group-wide and doesn't show a site. Strategic Operations at a CDMO usually covers network capacity, site programs and integration, which is relevant now with three new sites joining. **Don't assume he owns process chemistry.** He said biocatalysis is not a need *to his knowledge*.

company.text: Siegfried (founded 1873, HQ **Zofingen**, Switzerland) is a CDMO that develops and manufactures **small-molecule drug substances** (APIs, intermediates, controlled substances) and **drug products** for pharma customers. CEO: **Marcel Imwinkelried**. **Eduardo Montanha** (ex-Fresenius Kabi) became the single group **COO** on Sep 1, 2026, after the Drug Substances and Drug Products COO roles were merged. Ramzahn's 'Strategic Operations' likely sits in this operations organisation (to be confirmed). In **May 2026** Siegfried closed the purchase of three drug substance sites from an SK Capital affiliate: **Noramco (Wilmington, DE)** for commercial-scale APIs, **Purisys (Athens, GA)** for clinical API development, and **Extractas (Tasmania, Australia)**. In **June 2026** it opened a new large-scale API plant in **Minden, Germany** (+100 m³ reactor capacity, including highly potent substances). Other drug substance sites include Pennsville NJ and Evionnaz CH.

financials.text: **FY2025:** net sales **CHF 1,327.8M** (+4.3% in local currencies); core EBITDA **CHF 312.3M** (23.5% margin); core net profit **CHF 162.1M**; CHF 0.40/share payout. **H1 2026:** net sales **CHF 633M** (+2.2%); core EBITDA **CHF 142M** (+6%, 22.4% margin); core net profit **CHF 68.2M**; free cash flow down to **CHF 15.1M** (acquisition and capex). **FY2026 outlook:** high-single-digit sales growth including the acquisition, core EBITDA margin above 23%. The acquired sites are expected to add about **$100M** of sales in 2026. Financially strong and investing. Margin focus makes **process efficiency** (fewer steps, lower cost of goods) the right pitch.

industry.title: Biocatalysis is now standard in API route design
industry.text: Big pharma and CDMOs increasingly use engineered enzymes for chiral steps and greener routes. CDMOs without in-house enzyme engineering often **partner** for it, which is where Enzymicals fits.

industry.title: CDMO consolidation and capacity race
industry.text: Siegfried is adding sites (US, Australia) and reactor volume (Minden). Winning high-volume projects means competing on **cost of goods and sustainability**, both areas where enzymatic steps help.

industry.title: Greener chemistry pressure
industry.text: Pharma customers push suppliers to cut solvent use and waste. Siegfried itself highlights optimised solvent use at its new Minden plant.

talking_points: Who at Siegfried owns **route scouting / process R&D** for drug substances, and does any site already run enzymatic steps?
With **Wilmington and Athens** now on board, are customers asking for greener or shorter routes on high-volume APIs?
Would a **one-route feasibility screen** (enzyme screening + first engineering round) be easy to approve as a small project?
How does Siegfried handle **tech transfer** from external partners into its plants? Enzymicals can deliver a process package ready to scale.
Is there a **German or Swiss site** (Minden, Evionnaz, Zofingen) where an in-person meeting with the chemists would make sense?
